# API migration evidence

`domain-characterization.json` is the unchanged historical Mac characterization, not a promise of bitwise solver stopping across operating systems or numerical libraries. It continues to supply direct aggregation/sharing/scientific-control fixtures.

`benchmark-3ec62f68.py.txt` is the exact original `src/fedference/benchmark.py` at commit `3ec62f68f08b03dc22323fa4e8a67b0c87be894e`; `benchmark-reference.json` binds its SHA-256. Tests execute its original CSV-loading entry point and original benchmark body in the same interpreter as the current explicit-input boundary, comparing every report value and type exactly, including iteration counts. No tolerance or allowed count range is used. Changed reference bytes, current parameters, report fields and diagnostics must be rejected.

The two implementations share aggregation primitives. This establishes boundary/report migration parity; it is not independent mathematical replication, cross-platform bitwise reproducibility, scientific validation or permission to change solver defaults. Existing primitive and solver-budget tests remain separate. Historical Linux results of 16 and 13 against the Mac value 15 remain retained failures of the original cross-runtime golden assertion.

`sharing-3ec62f68.py.txt` and `sharing-reference.json` bind the original belief-sharing orchestration at the same commit. Its full result is compared in the same interpreter, with exact arrays, dtypes, values, report shape and integer diagnostics. The direct aggregation/scientific-control fixtures remain unchanged. The original module is loaded under a private test name for dataclass resolution; production modules are never replaced. Changed parameters, diagnostics and original bytes must refuse. It shares production aggregation primitives and does not establish independent mathematics or cross-platform bitwise convergence.
